claims.text: The briefing answers 'Is there the potential for commercial use' with 'YES', citing the design of energy generation machinery with power output levels much higher than those currently achievable by conventional means.

claims.nodeLabel: NAVAIR Invention Disclosure Briefing, Navy Case PAX 205 (Inertial Mass Reduction Device)
claims.text: Its 'Description of Invention' slide asserts that 'It is possible to reduce the inertial mass and hence the gravitational mass, of a system/object in motion, by an abrupt perturbation of the non-linear background of local Spacetime', with the mechanism attributed to negative pressure in a polarized local vacuum energy state achieved by coupling accelerated high frequency vibration with accelerated high frequency axial spin of an electrically charged object.

claims.nodeLabel: NAVAIR Invention Disclosure Briefing, Navy Case PAX 205 (Inertial Mass Reduction Device)
claims.text: The document is a six-page Navy briefing headed 'INERTIAL MASS REDUCTION DEVICE, Navy Case PAX 205', released by NAVAIR under FOIA case 2021-003244.

claims.sourceText: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, PAX 205 briefing, slide 3
claims.text: The PAX 205 briefing opens by quoting VADM Paul Grosklags, Commander NAVAIR, dated 11-19-2015, and frames the device as delivering 'Battlefield Supremacy, against all foes'.

claims.sourceText: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, PAX 205 briefing, slides 4 and 5
claims.text: The PAX 205 briefing states the hybrid craft 'would move with great ease through the air / space / water mediums, by being enclosed in a Vacuum plasma bubble/sheath', and that 'Energy flux values of 10^33 Watts/m^2 (and beyond) are possible.'

claims.sourceText: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, PAX 205 briefing, slide 5
claims.text: The PAX 205 briefing states that 'it is possible to use the IMRD as an artificial gravitational wave generator (invention enables Gertsenshtein Effect)', that this 'has tremendous air and space military implications and applications (both offensive and defensive in nature)', and that 'Local spacetime modification on a grand scale (planetary-size disruption) is thus feasible.'

claims.sourceText: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, PAX 205 briefing, slide 5
claims.text: The PAX 205 briefing states the invention 'makes possible the design of a hybrid aerospace / undersea craft (HAUC), which due to the physical mechanisms enabled with the Inertial Mass Reduction Device (IMRD), can function as a submersible craft capable of extreme aerial and underwater speeds (lack of air/water-skin friction) and enhanced stealth capabilities (non-linear scattering of RF and sonar signals).'

claims.sourceText: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, 'PAX 205 - INERTIAL MASS REDUCTION DEVICE', p. 1, https://www.navair.navy.mil/foia/sites/g/files/jejdrs566/files/document/%5Bfilename%5D/2021-003244%20FINAL%20VERSION%20PAX%20205%20-%20INERTIAL%20MASS%20REDUCTION%20DEVICE.pdf
claims.text: The Navy invention-disclosure briefing for Navy Case PAX 205 identifies its author as 'Salvatore Cezar Pais, Ph.D., Department of Defense / Department of the Navy, Naval Air Systems Command / NAWCAD, NAS Patuxent River Maryland 20670', with competency code 4.4.5.1 and a salvatore.pais@navy.mil address.

claims.sourceText: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, PAX 205 briefing, slide 6
claims.text: The PAX 205 briefing proposes Section 219 NISE funding of 250,000 USD in anticipated labour and 250,000 USD in anticipated NAWCAD facility cost for experimental investigation of the concept, under a slide headed 'EXPERIMENT TRUMPS THEORY EVERYTIME!'

claims.locator: slides 4-5; the board's inference from it
claims.sourceText: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, PAX 205 briefing, slides 4-5, compared against the reported characteristics on this board
claims.text: The PAX 205 description of a single craft combining transmedium air/space/water travel, extreme speed without skin friction, and low observability through non-linear scattering of RF and sonar tracks the flight characteristics reported by Navy aircrew in the same period more closely than any other document in the federal patent record. Reasoning: direct comparison of the briefing's own capability list against the reported characteristics; the correspondence is a matter of textual overlap and does not establish a causal direction in either direction.

claims.sourceText: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, 'PAX 205 - INERTIAL MASS REDUCTION DEVICE', slides 4-5, https://www.navair.navy.mil/foia/sites/g/files/jejdrs566/files/document/%5Bfilename%5D/2021-003244%20FINAL%20VERSION%20PAX%20205%20-%20INERTIAL%20MASS%20REDUCTION%20DEVICE.pdf
claims.text: Four of the five are itemised as design goals in a United States Navy invention-disclosure briefing released under FOIA. The PAX 205 briefing describes a 'hybrid aerospace / undersea craft (HAUC)' that 'would move with great ease through the air / space / water mediums' (trans-medium travel), enclosed in a 'Vacuum plasma bubble/sheath' giving extreme speed without skin friction (hypersonic velocity), with non-linear scattering of radio frequency and sonar signals (low observability), by means of an inertial mass reduction device (lift without flight surfaces). This is the whole reason the taxonomy is on this board.

claims.locator: slides 4-5; the board's inference from it
claims.sourceText: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, PAX 205 briefing, slides 4-5, read against the five as published
claims.text: The fifth observable, sudden and instantaneous acceleration, is NOT itemised as a design goal in the PAX 205 briefing. The briefing speaks of operating the device 'under rapid acceleration transients' as a means of generating the field, which is a statement about how the machine is driven rather than a claimed flight characteristic of the craft. Recorded because four out of five is the accurate figure and five would be the easy overclaim.
